For this task I made a unit converter that changes kilometres into miles and miles into
kilometres. I picked it because I run every weekend and the running app I use shows distances in
miles, which I find confusing.

What worked: the maths is simple once you know that one mile is exactly 1.609344 kilometres. I
wrote two small functions, one for each direction, and checked them against a table of distances
from a printed race guide. The results matched to three decimal places. I also made a simple web
page with a picture of a running track and a short text about my favourite races, and that page
is online now at the demo link.

What did not work: I wanted the web page to do the conversion too, but I could not get the form to
send the number to the Python code, so for now the converter only runs from the command line. I
also tried to add yards and feet, but I kept mixing up the factors, so I took them out again. My
repository is still private because I was not sure whether I was allowed to share it, and I did
not have time to ask before the deadline.

Next week I would like to learn how a web form talks to a program, so that the page and the
converter work together, and then add more units once the first two are reliable.
